title: Capetian House of Anjou
capsule: The Capetian House of Anjou was founded by Charles I (1226–1285), youngest brother of Louis IX of France, who received Anjou as an apanage in 1246 and conquered the Kingdom of Sicily by defeating Manfred of Sicily at the Battle of Benevento in 1266. The Sicilian Vespers revolt of 1282 expelled the Angevins from the island of Sicily, which passed to Aragon, but the dynasty retained the Regno (southern Italy) as the Kingdom of Naples, which remained the principal Angevin holding. Various cadet branches ruled Hungary (1308–1395), Poland, and the principality of Achaea simultaneously, making the house one of the most ramified dynastic networks of 14th-century Europe. The main Neapolitan line ended with Queen Joanna I's murder in 1382 and was disputed thereafter until the Aragonese takeover in 1442.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Italian holdings are well documented; the simultaneous territories of cadet branches in Hungary and Poland are attested but cartographically complex to represent as a single extent.
